title: Differential pad budgeting and hierarchical bucketizer for micro-batch shaping
creator: Emma Chen
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: end-to-end packing with synthetic mixed-length traces reduces padded tokens by >=10% compared to baseline packer (same seqlen distribution used in previous benchmarks)
Latency SLOs: p95 latency change <= +3% and p99 latency change <= +7% for hosted API mainline traffic in canary run
Throughput: no drop in sustained throughput greater than 5% on Dedicated small cluster workloads
Observability: new metrics emitted (pad_budget_assigned, pad_reclaimed, bucket_assignment, kernel_hint) and dashboards created
Rollout: staged canary (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback hook on latency or error increases
progress_updates: 2026-01-26: Kickoff meeting with infra, serving-runtime, and kernels team. Agreed on 3-tier bucket strategy and pad budget signals to emit.
2026-02-02: Prototype pad-budget estimator implemented (Python) and integrated with local packer. Initial synthetic tests show 6-9% pad reduction on mixed traces.
2026-02-12: Kernel hinting API sketched; submitted RFC to kernel-team. Decided to use lightweight enum hints (SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE) rather than exact kernel ids to keep scheduler flexible.
2026-02-18: Implemented first pass of hierarchical bucketizer in Rust packer. Microbench harness indicates 12% pad token reduction for user-simulated conversational traces with low attention density.
2026-02-22: Stress test on Dedicated staging cluster revealed memory fragmentation for batches with many SMALL-kernel selections on A100; working with infra to add transient allocator tuning.
2026-02-28: Canary flag wired; planning 1% traffic canary next week. Drafted dashboards and alert rules for pad_reclaimed ratio, p95/p99 latency deltas, and GPU utilization per bucket.
comments: Luca Moretti (2026-02-03): Prototype looks promising — need to add telemetry hooks so we can correlate pad budget decisions with downstream kernel performance.
Aisha Patel (Design, 2026-02-05): UX note — include per-route toggle in Console to enable 'aggressive pad trimming' so customers can opt-in for cost savings with explicit throughput trade-off.
Rajat Singh (Kernels, 2026-02-13): Kernel hinting enum OK. Kernel team will accept hints but reserves right to override if memory layout or kernel fails internal preconditions.
QA (2026-02-20): Add fuzz tests for extreme seqlen skew and adversarial small-batch bursts to ensure there is no p99 regression under pathological traffic.
Product (2026-02-24): Target customers for early access: two PLG customers with heavy chat workloads and one enterprise on Dedicated; coordinate with Solutions Eng for outreach.
